input.reasoning_summary:
All three challenges have been refuted by the evidence:

H1 (Other components contributing equally or more): Evidence E3 shows that for the quarter ended December 31, 2025, Productivity and Business Processes revenue increased $4.7 billion total. Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services contributed $3.4 billion of this increase (72% of the total growth). In contrast, Microsoft 365 Consumer contributed only $484 million and LinkedIn contributed $456 million. Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud was clearly the dominant contributor.

H2 (On-premises products as primary driver): Evidence E3 shows Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud grew 17% while Microsoft 365 Commercial products grew only 13%. The cloud component grew faster and, given the overall revenue base, contributed more to the growth than on-premises products.

H3 (Other primary drivers identified): Evidence E2 explicitly states that Productivity and Business Processes revenue increase was "driven by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud" - identifying it as the primary driver without mentioning other equally important drivers.

The initial verdict of SUPPORTED remains correct. The filing explicitly attributes the Productivity and Business Processes revenue growth in Q2 FY2026 to Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud, and the quantitative breakdown confirms this was indeed the primary driver, contributing the vast majority of the segment's growth.
